attempted_axis: EXTERN-RETYPE TU pass over src/game/game/combat.c: swap the two shadowing untyped externs (`extern u8 gPlayers[]`, `extern u8* gCurLevel`) for the GC-verified header types (Player, level_data -- both headers already included by this TU), then convert the sites the retype unblocks while leaving every gCameraState supervisor-blob access raw per the work order.

attributes.law_screen: claim.law.gCameraState-blob-vs-typed-camera-base: APPLIED, decisive -- this TU's dominant raw-offset cluster is InitCamera's 82 `cs + N` sites plus `gcs`/`cameraState` walks in init_game_cam(6), cam_orient_to(3), ProcCamera(3), recalc_lookat(1), i.e. ~95 of the TU's 179 bare sites are gCameraState-blob walks past the symbol's true 52-byte boundary. The law requires a per-function fnasm relocation check before renaming any of them, and the work order independently reserves them for a later shared-cameradata.h wave; ALL were left raw and untouched. The law's safe half also held: the `&gCameras[idx]`-derived `Camera* cam` pointers already use named members and were not disturbed. claim.law.noop-cast-on-array-decay-not-neutral (discovered this session in gamemain.c): APPLIED as a screen -- combat.c's one alias-assignment site `u8* p = gPlayers;` was identified in advance as the risky shape, gated explicitly, and came back byte-identical, establishing the counter-example that makes that law site-specific rather than shape-specific. claim.law.recomputed-index-array-form-safe: APPLIED -- MissileCollidePlayer's `(Player*)(gPlayers + i * PLAYER_STRIDE)` is a fresh per-iteration recompute (no carried `+=`), so it converted to `&gPlayers[i]`; gated byte-identical. claim.law.offsetof-rename-preserves-protected-web: APPLIED -- the two Player field reads in the case-1 scan loop became offsetof addends on the still-raw walked pointer; byte-identical. claim.law.multifield-alias-defeats-indexed-addressing: SCREENED, respected -- that walked `p` touches two nearby fields (state, vibe_on) so it kept its raw-pointer + offsetof form and was never given a typed alias. claim.law.sizeof-defeats-loop-stride-induction: SCREENED, respected -- PLAYER_STRIDE stayed a bare 0x335C literal; no sizeof() substitution anywhere. claim.law.embedded-struct-member-whole-tu-cascade: SCREENED, not applicable -- no header edited. claim.law.lwzu-idiom-web-retention: SCREENED, no load-update web touched.
attributes.residual: 172 bare sites remain (from 179). The retype itself was nearly free here because this TU defines `PF(base, off, type) (*(type*)((u8*)(base) + (off)))` and already spells most globals through explicit casts -- gCurLevel needed ZERO neutralizing edits (all 13 of its sites already went through `(u8*)`, `(char*)`, `*(u32*)` or PF), so its retype was a pure declaration change plus 8 optional member-form cleanups. Left raw, with reasons: (1) ~95 gCameraState supervisor-blob sites -- RESERVED for the shared cameradata.h wave, not a failure (see law screen). (2) screen_limitation's 13 `item`/`info`/`record` sites: these ARE convertible (Item.minplayers@0xCC and Item.data[0x14]@0xDC exist in game/item.h; `record` is an `iteminfo` walked at stride 0x50 with its `iteminfodata item` sub-struct at +4) but were deliberately not attempted this pass -- the function carries a live STRUCTURAL cap (attempt.screen-limitation-debug-mask-fold.20260830.v1) on a different axis, the reads cross an iteminfo/iteminfodata nesting boundary that needs a `record + offsetof(iteminfo,item) + offsetof(iteminfodata,...)` two-level addend form, and the extern-retype lane's remaining budget was better spent on gamemain's larger Player/Enemy clusters. This is the cheapest well-understood next chunk in this TU and is handed off ready. (3) StandardCamera/get_cam_dist's `t` = `(CameraTarget*)(cameraState + 0xA10)` -- a gCameraState-derived base, so it inherits the same reservation as (1).
